question: What do you call a proportionate saving in costs gained by an increased level of production?
solution:
The correct answer is "__**Economies of scale**__"

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **Economies of scale **

 __
 
• It refers to the **cost advantage experienced by a firm** when it** increases its level of output**
 
• The **advantage arises due to the inverse relationship between the per-unit fixed cost and the quantity **produced.
 
• The **greater the quantity of output produced**, the lower the **per-unit fixed cost.**
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/9de4c2dc69ee162cc735953a40c53487ce402085b9ea79998907e1b4ddf215ea.png] 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Isocost**-A curve s**howing the combinations of factor inputs that have constant market cost**
 
• **Isoquant **-An isoquant **shows all combinations of factors that produce a certain output**
 
• **Production function**
 
 
• It is an **​equation** that expresses the **relationship between the quantities of productive factors (such as labour and capital) used and the amount of product obtained.** 
 
• It **states the amount of product that can be obtained from every combination of factors, assuming that the most efficient available methods of production are used.**
